title: Hal Higdon Advanced 5K Training Program (8 weeks)
population: Experienced 5K runners who already run 4-5 days a week and 20-30+ miles weekly (6 run days per week in the plan)
findings: Sunday long run is set by time: 60, 65, 70 min in weeks 1-3, 5K test race in week 4, then 75, 85, 90 min in weeks 5-7; week 8 is the 5K race.
Typical week is 6 run days and 1 day off: Monday 3 mi easy, Tuesday 200 m or 400 m repeats, Thursday 30-45 min tempo, Saturday 4-6 mi fast run.
Peak long run is 90 min; the page header lists a longest workout of 12 miles, which does not match the 90 min schedule and is treated as unreliable.
limitations: Read through a page-fetch summariser; the header 'longest workout 12 miles' is inconsistent with the schedule. Convention, not evidence. Year is the access date.
implications: Established advanced 5K plan peaks the long run at 90 min for runners at 20-30+ miles per week, above the engine's current 60 min 5K cap; supports raising the 5K high-volume cap toward 75-90 min.
Long run is time-based, matching the engine's minutes convention; progression is +5 min per step, with a +10 min step in week 6.
